findings.quote: "command": "aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources --tag-filters Key=task,Values=containers-t03 --query \"ResourceTagMappingList[].ResourceARN\"", "expect": "An empty list. If the task definition ARN still shows, ECS has not finished the deletion: wait one minute and run the command again. findings.type: technical: verify step that cannot reliably prove the cleanup
findings.evidence: Saved page docs/resourcegroupstagging/latest/APIReference/API_GetResources: "Returns all the tagged or previously tagged resources that are located in the specified AWS Region for the account." The ECS guide (full:amazonecs-developerguide, Amazon ECS task definition states) says: "After the task definition is in the DELETE_IN_PROGRESS state, Amazon ECS periodically verifies that the target task definition is not being referenced by any active tasks or deployments, and then deletes the task definition permanently." and "Task definitions that are in the DELETE_IN_PROGRESS state can be viewed in the console and you can retrieve the task definition by calling DescribeTaskDefinition." No page gives a time for the permanent delete, so "wait one minute" is invented, and both checks can keep showing the revision after a correct cleanup (the reader then thinks the cleanup failed). Fix: verify with aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition $TD_ARN --query taskDefinition.status, expect DELETE_IN_PROGRESS (or an error once the delete is final), which proves the delete request was accepted.
findings.resolution: fix-19: the verify expect no longer invents a wait time. It now says: an empty list, or the ARN while ECS still holds the revision for deletion; the tagging API can also list previously tagged resources; then 'aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition $TD_ARN --query taskDefinition.status' shows DELETE_IN_PROGRESS, which proves that ECS accepted the delete. The verify command is unchanged, so the CLI check report (T113, commands hash) stays valid. tasks lint clean.
